qti-assessment-test.title: RealEstateCoach.com - Written Buyer-Broker Agreements & Listing Objection Scenarios (DigitalChalk SCORM 1.2 Demo)

qti-assessment-item.title: Execute compliant written buyer agreements prior to residential property tours.

qti-item-body.p: Objective: Execute compliant written buyer agreements prior to residential property tours.

qti-choice-interaction.qti-prompt: A relocating buyer calls from outside an open house and asks you to unlock a vacant listing down the street in 20 minutes. You have not signed a representation agreement yet. Which step keeps the tour compliant?
qti-choice-interaction.qti-simple-choice: Execute a signed written touring or buyer-representation agreement specifying an exact, negotiable fee term (even $0 for a single-day tour agreement) before entering the property.
Unlock the home immediately as a Ministerial Act and have the buyer sign the representation form before submitting an offer.
Have the buyer sign a quick form stating your fee will be 'whatever cooperative compensation the seller offers between 2% and 3%'.
Record a verbal consent text message from the buyer confirming your brokerage disclosures and follow up with paperwork that evening.

qti-content-body.p: Correct. A signed written agreement with a specific, non-open-ended compensation term and negotiability disclosure must precede any live property tour.
Incorrect. Touring a prospective buyer inside a listing triggers the pre-tour written agreement requirement well before offer submission.
Incorrect. Open-ended ranges or 'whatever the seller offers' clauses fail the objectively ascertainable compensation rule.
Incorrect. Informal text acknowledgments without the required written agreement clauses and negotiability language do not satisfy pre-tour compliance.

qti-assessment-item.title: Handle commission-negotiability questions accurately during listing consultations.

qti-item-body.p: Objective: Handle commission-negotiability questions accurately during listing consultations.

qti-choice-interaction.qti-prompt: During a listing appointment, the seller asks: 'Isn't the standard brokerage commission in our county fixed at 6%?' What is the legally compliant, high-trust response?
qti-choice-interaction.qti-simple-choice: Clarify immediately that real estate commissions are never fixed by law or MLS rule and are 100% negotiable, then walk through your specific marketing scope and service tiers.
Confirm that most top brokerages in the county charge 6% so pricing lower could discourage buyer agents from showing the home.
Tell the seller the local association sets a 3% minimum on the listing side while the buyer side is optional.
Defer the fee conversation until after the seller signs the exclusive listing agreement and photography is scheduled.

qti-content-body.p: Correct. Stating plainly that fees are never standardized or set by law avoids antitrust violations while anchoring your fee discussion in concrete seller services.
Incorrect. Implying local fee uniformity or warning of coordinated showing boycotts creates severe antitrust and steering exposure.
Incorrect. Associations and MLS boards never set minimum commission rates; stating otherwise is a material misrepresentation.
Incorrect. Compensation terms and negotiability disclosures must be agreed in writing as part of the listing contract itself.

qti-assessment-item.title: Maintain Fair Housing Act compliance when buyers ask subjective neighborhood questions.

qti-item-body.p: Objective: Maintain Fair Housing Act compliance when buyers ask subjective neighborhood questions.

qti-choice-interaction.qti-prompt: A buyer couple asks during a consultation: 'Which elementary school zones have the best families and lowest crime?' Which response protects both the client and Fair Housing compliance?
qti-choice-interaction.qti-simple-choice: Explain Fair Housing boundaries clearly, ask for their objective housing criteria (commute time, lot size, price), and share direct links to official municipal crime maps and state school report cards.
Recommend two suburban subdivisions where most of your relocating families with young children chose to buy last quarter.
Rank the neighborhoods personally from 'A' to 'D' for safety based on local word of mouth.
Refuse to answer any location questions and tell the buyers you can only unlock specific street addresses they email you.

qti-content-body.p: Correct. Redirecting to objective housing features and verifiable public data empowers the buyer's independent choice without demographic steering.
Incorrect. Directing buyers based on familial status demographics constitutes unlawful steering under the Fair Housing Act.
Incorrect. Subjective agent safety rankings act as unlawful proxies for protected-class neighborhood composition.
Incorrect. Agents can and should provide objective market data and links to authoritative public resources while explaining Fair Housing rules.
